title: い- and な-adjectives
titleJp: たかい 山、しずかな まち
canDo: I can describe things, places and people with い- and な-adjectives in the present: この まちは しずかです。
I can make an adjective negative the right way for its type: たかくないです (い) and しずかじゃないです (な).
I can say "it's not good" with the irregular form よくないです.
I can spot the な-adjectives that end in い (きれい, ゆうめい, きらい) and I don't conjugate them like い-adjectives.
I can put an adjective before a noun (たかい 山, しずかな まち) and ask どんな 〜ですか。

blocks.t: Warm-up: make 3 nouns negative with じゃないです (lesson 02-3) and read this lesson's vocabulary (block 3) aloud
Vocabulary: tap 🔊 on each adjective, repeat it twice and copy it into your notebook in two columns (い / な)
Grammar: the 3 points, each with its examples read aloud and one 🔬
Lesson 5 video (block 6): only the part on the present tense and on adjectives before nouns
Notebook homework + checking it against the answer key
Checklist (block 10) + write your questions in the lesson notebook

skills: Making nouns negative with じゃないです (lesson 02-3): な-adjectives become negative the same way.
Using この / その / あの + noun (lesson 02-1), which appears in almost every example.
Reading hiragana fluently. The adjectives stay in kana in this lesson, because Genki only introduces their kanji in later lessons.

vocab.en: expensive; tall, high (a mountain, a building)
good (irregular negative: よくないです)
pretty, beautiful; clean (a な-adjective, despite the final い)
famous (a な-adjective, despite the final い)
what kind of… (always before a noun)

grammar.title: い-adjectives: 〜いです / 〜くないです
grammar.explanation:
An adjective is a word that says **what something is like**: expensive, new, fun. Japanese has two types of adjectives, and the type decides how the adjective changes. The first type ends in **い** (たかい, おもしろい, あたらしい) and **conjugates by itself**: the adjective itself turns negative.
• Affirmative: adjective + です → たかいです ("it's expensive").
• Negative: drop the final い and add **くないです** → たか|い → たか|くないです ("it isn't expensive"). You will also hear たかくありません, with the same meaning and a slightly more formal tone.
• With い-adjectives, です only makes the sentence polite: the meaning "is" is already inside the adjective. That is why the adjective carries the negative, and です stays as it is.
• In the sentence, adjective + です is the **PREDICATE**: it sits at the end, and it is where you start reading. The block with は is the TOPIC, the thing being described: この とけいは | たかいです。
• Important exception: **いい** (good). The affirmative is いいです, but the negative comes from よい, another form of the same word: **よくないです**. Never いくないです.
grammar.structure: [N] は [い-adj]です。 · [N] は [adj minus い]くないです。

examples.jp: にほんごの しゅくだいは むずかしいです。
examples.kana: にほんごの しゅくだいは むずかしいです。
examples.romaji: Nihongo no shukudai wa muzukashii desu.

examples.jp: マリアさんの へやは あたらしいですか。— いいえ、あたらしくないです。
examples.kana: マリアさんの へやは あたらしいですか。— いいえ、あたらしくないです。
examples.romaji: Maria-san no heya wa atarashii desu ka. — Iie, atarashikunai desu.
examples.en: Is Maria's room new? — No, it isn't new.

examples.jp: きょうの 天気は よくないです。
examples.kana: きょうの てんきは よくないです。
examples.romaji: Kyō no tenki wa yokunai desu.

pitfalls: い-adjectives don't use じゃないです: たかいじゃないです ✗ → たかくないです ✓. The adjective itself becomes negative.
Drop the い before adding くない: たかいくないです ✗ → たかくないです ✓.
いい is irregular in the negative: いくないです ✗ → よくないです ✓.
Japanese has no dummy "it": "It's cold today" is not それは さむいです ✗ → きょうは さむいです ✓. The adjective + です already says "is cold".
howToStudy: Make a table in your notebook with 8 い-adjectives: 〜いです in column 1, 〜くないです in column 2. Read both columns aloud, and include いい → よくないです.

Tap 🔬 on example 2. マリアさんの shows up as DESCRIBES NEXT (it describes へや), へやは is the TOPIC (the thing described) and あたらしいですか is the PREDICATE. Read the predicate first ("is it new?"), then ask: what is? In the answer, the topic is dropped: あたらしくないです alone is the PREDICATE.
Describe 5 objects in your home aloud, with one affirmative and one negative sentence each: この とけいは ふるいです。たかくないです。

grammar.title: な-adjectives: 〜です / 〜じゃないです
grammar.gloss: adjectives that act like nouns at the end of a sentence
grammar.explanation:
The second type is the **な-adjectives** (しずか, にぎやか, 元気, ゆうめい). At the end of a sentence they behave **like nouns**: the adjective stays the same and only です changes.
• Affirmative: しずかです ("it's quiet").
• Negative: しずか**じゃないです** ("it isn't quiet"), just like がくせいじゃないです in lesson 02-3. しずかじゃありません also exists, with the same meaning.
• At the end of a sentence there is **no な**: しずかです. な only appears when the adjective comes before a noun (point c).

**な-adjectives that end in い.** A few な-adjectives happen to end in い: **きれい** (pretty, clean), **ゆうめい** (famous) and **きらい** (disliked, lesson 05-2). That い is part of the word, not the ending of an い-adjective. So the negative is きれいじゃないです, never きれくないです.
• Clue: if the word ends in **-ei** (きれい = kirei, ゆうめい = yūmei), it is a な-adjective. The い-adjectives at this level end in -ai, -ii, -ui or -oi (たかい, おおきい, ふるい, おもしろい).
• きらい ends in -ai, like たかい, so the clue doesn't help there. Just memorize that one.
• In this lesson's vocabulary and in Genki's word lists, な-adjectives are marked (な): きれい(な). Learn each adjective together with its type.
grammar.structure: [N] は [な-adj] です。 · [N] は [な-adj] じゃないです。

examples.jp: リオは にぎやかです。
examples.kana: リオは にぎやかです。

examples.jp: この 川は きれいじゃないです。
examples.kana: この かわは きれいじゃないです。
examples.romaji: Kono kawa wa kirei ja nai desu.

examples.jp: その レストランは ゆうめいですか。— いいえ、ゆうめいじゃないです。
examples.kana: その レストランは ゆうめいですか。— いいえ、ゆうめいじゃないです。
examples.romaji: Sono resutoran wa yūmei desu ka. — Iie, yūmei ja nai desu.
examples.en: Is that restaurant famous? — No, it isn't.

pitfalls: きれい and ゆうめい are な-adjectives: きれくないです ✗ → きれいじゃないです ✓; ゆうめくないです ✗ → ゆうめいじゃないです ✓.
No な at the end of a sentence: しずかなです ✗ → しずかです ✓.
Don't mix the two systems: にぎやかくないです ✗ → にぎやかじゃないです ✓. A な-adjective never takes く.
To say "I'm fine" (お元気ですか。— …), use 元気, not いい: いいです ✗ → はい、元気です ✓. Before a noun, 元気な 人 means "an energetic person".
howToStudy: Sort all of this lesson's vocabulary into two columns, い and な. Highlight きれい and ゆうめい: they end in -ei and are な.
Tap 🔬 on the river example. この shows up as DESCRIBES NEXT, 川は is the TOPIC and きれいじゃないです is the PREDICATE. Notice that きれい did not change: only です became じゃないです.
Say 4 sentences aloud about your town, 2 affirmative and 2 negative, with しずか, にぎやか, きれい and ゆうめい.

grammar.title: Adjective + noun: たかい 山, しずかな まち
grammar.explanation:
To describe a noun inside a sentence, the adjective comes **before** it — the same order as in English: "a tall mountain" → たかい 山.
• い-adjectives go straight in, with nothing in between: おもしろい えいが, あたらしい とけい.
• な-adjectives: this is where the **な** appears. しずかな まち, きれいな 川, ゆうめいな 人. This な is where the name "な-adjective" comes from.
• Don't put の between an adjective and a noun. の links a noun to a noun (lesson 01-1): にほんごの せんせい, but おもしろい せんせい.
• The block [adjective + noun] works as **a single noun**. It can be a topic, an object, a place, or come before です. In サンパウロは おおきい まちです。, the predicate is おおきい まちです ("is a big city"): 🔬 shows おおきい as DESCRIBES NEXT, attached to まち, and まちです as the PREDICATE.
• To ask "what kind of…?", use **どんな** + noun: どんな まちですか。 The answer puts an adjective where どんな was: しずかな まちです。
grammar.structure: [い-adj] [N] · [な-adj] な [N] · どんな [N] ですか。

examples.jp: サンパウロは おおきい まちです。
examples.kana: サンパウロは おおきい まちです。
examples.en: São Paulo is a big city.

examples.jp: ふじ山は どんな 山ですか。— たかい 山です。
examples.kana: ふじさんは どんな やまですか。— たかい やまです。
examples.romaji: Fujisan wa donna yama desu ka. — Takai yama desu.
examples.en: What kind of mountain is Mt. Fuji? — It's a tall mountain.

examples.jp: きのう、にぎやかな レストランで ばんごはんを 食べました。
examples.kana: きのう、にぎやかな レストランで ばんごはんを たべました。
examples.romaji: Kinō, nigiyaka na resutoran de bangohan o tabemashita.
examples.en: Yesterday I had dinner at a lively restaurant.

pitfalls: な-adjectives need な before a noun: しずか まち ✗ → しずかな まち ✓. And い-adjectives never take な: たかいな 山 ✗ → たかい 山 ✓.
Don't use の with an adjective: おもしろいの えいが ✗ → おもしろい えいが ✓.
The な-adjectives that end in い take な too: きれい 川 ✗ → きれいな 川 ✓; ゆうめい 人 ✗ → ゆうめいな 人 ✓.
です goes only at the very end, never between the adjective and the noun: おおきいです まちです ✗ → おおきい まちです ✓.
howToStudy: Drills → 🔬 Anatomy → 🧱 Build from the end with example 3: start with 食べました, then ばんごはんを, then レストランで, then にぎやかな, and finally きのう. Notice that にぎやかな always sits right before レストラン: it DESCRIBES NEXT.
Write 6 real pairs in your notebook (3 with い, 3 with な) about your own things: あたらしい スマホ, しずかな へや, ふるい とけい…
Ask どんな まちですか aloud about 3 places you know, and answer with adjective + noun. A detail in example 2: in ふじ山 the kanji 山 is read さん — a reading of the kanji, not the さん of たなかさん.

homework.intro: Do it by hand in your notebook. Write the adjectives in kana; use kanji only for the words that appeared in this lesson (山, 川, 天気, 元気, 人…). Only then open the answer key, item by item. Circle what you got wrong and redo it the next day.

tasks.prompt: Make each sentence negative (polite style). Before writing, decide: い or な?

items.note: い: drop the い and add くないです. The ありません forms are also correct, with the same meaning: たかくありません, and for な-adjectives しずかじゃありません (or しずかではありません).
な: the adjective stays the same; only です becomes じゃないです.
Exception: the negative comes from よい.
きれい is a な-adjective: it ends in -ei.

tasks.prompt: Join the adjective to the noun. Add な where it's needed; where it isn't, just write the two words side by side.

items.note: A な-adjective: it needs な.
An い-adjective: it goes straight in, with nothing in between.

items.q: ゆうめい＿ レストラン

a.jp: ゆうめいな レストラン

items.q: あたらしい＿ とけい

a.jp: あたらしい とけい

items.note: きれい is a な-adjective, even though it ends in い.

items.q: つまらない＿ えいが

a.jp: つまらない えいが
この 山は たかくないです。
a.kana: この やまは たかくないです。

items.note: この 山は たかくありません。 is also correct.

a.jp: きょうは さむくないです。

items.note: No word for "it": the adjective + です is enough.

a.jp: この ほんは おもしろくないです。
マリアさんは ゆうめいな 人ですか。
a.kana: マリアさんは ゆうめいな ひとですか。
a.romaji: Maria-san wa yūmei na hito desu ka.

items.note: Adjective + noun before です; the な is required.

items.q: What kind of person is Professor Yamada? — An energetic person.

a.jp: 山田せんせいは どんな 人ですか。— 元気な 人です。
a.kana: やまだせんせいは どんな ひとですか。— げんきな ひとです。
a.romaji: Yamada-sensei wa donna hito desu ka. — Genki na hito desu.

items.note: The answer puts the adjective where どんな was.

tasks.prompt: Describe your town (or your neighborhood) in 4 sentences: 2 with the adjective at the end (one affirmative, one negative) and 2 with adjective + noun. Then read it aloud and record it on your phone.

items.q: Model (match its structure, not its words):

a.jp: わたしの まちは ちいさいです。にぎやかじゃないです。しずかな まちです。きれいな 川が あります。
a.kana: わたしの まちは ちいさいです。にぎやかじゃないです。しずかな まちです。きれいな かわが あります。
a.romaji: Watashi no machi wa chiisai desu. Nigiyaka ja nai desu. Shizuka na machi desu. Kirei na kawa ga arimasu.
a.en: My town is small. It isn't lively. It's a quiet town. There's a beautiful river.

items.note: Check: い-adjectives made negative with くないです, な-adjectives with じゃないです, な only before a noun, and the predicate always at the end.

workbook.tip: Do it after points a and b: it's the present-tense conjugation table.
Do it after point c. If an item asks for the past tense, leave it until after lesson 05-2. Check it with the official Genki Answer Key.

practice.what: Play normally. Whenever a line of dialogue has an adjective (〜いです, 〜くないです or an adjective before a noun), pause and say aloud whether it is い or な. Copy 2 of those lines into your notebook and underline the predicate.
Lesson 5 vocabulary in the SRS. Then Practice L5 → conjugation, only with the present-tense forms for now.
Drills → 🔬 Anatomy → 🏷 Tag: 5 sentences with adjectives. Check that you find the PREDICATE and can say which block DESCRIBES NEXT.
Tap 🔊 on each example in this lesson and repeat along 3 times. In the negatives, keep the rhythm even: た・か・く・な・い・で・す is 7 beats of the same length.
Record the description of your town (homework h4) in 30 seconds or less. Listen and check that each negative used the right form for its type.

culture.title: The sense of season: はなみ and seasonal food
culture.titleJp: はなみ と しゅん
culture.body: Japan pays a lot of attention to the changing seasons, and it shows in everyday life. In spring the cherry blossoms (さくら) last only a short time, and many people do **はなみ**: a picnic under the trees with friends, family or coworkers. Weather forecasts usually show when the flowers should open in each region, because the blooming generally starts in the south and moves north. Food follows the calendar too: each ingredient has its **しゅん**, the time of year when it tastes best, and shops and restaurants often sell limited-edition seasonal products (きせつげんてい). Autumn, for example, often brings chestnuts and sweet potatoes to mind, and winter brings みかん and hot-pot dishes (なべ).
culture.try: Describe the current season where you live in 3 sentences, using this lesson's adjectives (いまは あついです。…). Then think of a fruit that is in season there and say what it's like: 〜は おおきいです / やすいです…

checklist: I can sort this lesson's adjectives into い and な without looking, including きれい and ゆうめい (な).
I make い-adjectives negative with 〜くないです and な-adjectives with 〜じゃないです.
I say よくないです (not いくないです) for "it's not good".
I put the adjective before the noun, with な only for な-adjectives: たかい 山, しずかな まち.
I can ask どんな 〜ですか and answer with adjective + noun.
I did the homework, checked it against the answer key and redid what I got wrong.
